rationale:
Positives: The agent verified identity correctly using full name + zip, pulled the correct account and orders, and targeted the DC-address order (#W5270061). It also looked up valid product variants and successfully modified the backpack to medium grey polyester and the desk lamp to black.

Critical failures against policy: 
- The agent executed order-changing writes (item modifications and an additional gift card charge for the price difference) without first stating the exact changes and obtaining explicit user confirmation. This violates the requirement to confirm before any order-changing write.
- The agent then attempted an address update after modifying items; the system rejected it because the order status changed to a non-pending state (“pending (item modified)”). This sequencing blocked the user’s requested address change; the agent neither warned the user beforehand nor sought confirmation that proceeding with item changes might prevent further modifications.
- When the user asked to pay with a gift card, the agent incorrectly stated that changing payment was not possible, failing to note that the order was already paid via gift card and that an additional gift card charge had already been applied. This is inaccurate final information.
- The agent also did not provide a confirmation step before attempting the address change once the user supplied the address, as required.

Given these issues—especially performing writes without confirmation and providing incorrect information about payment—the interaction does not meet the pass bar.
